Phase 1. 478,234 transitions from 7,985 rides -> 38,351 edges at >=2 transitions, 21,130 nodes, LCC 93.9%. Phase 2 found the caveat: at 18 chars it is a bundle of corridors, not a network - 2,025 independent loops exist but every tested O-D pair has exactly ONE corridor. Phase 2. rider_dna skill is peak lean PER CORNER (p95 30.2 deg); cell demand_p90 is the p90 over every sample in a cell, straights included (median 7.4 deg). route_loop(): Dijkstra out + a second on the TRANSPOSED graph for the time back; feasible turnarounds ranked by fit cost per second; ride out, make the used edges 6x expensive, route home so the return finds different roads. Orienteering is NP-hard so this is a heuristic and says so. 16/16 of 4 starts x {1,1.5,2,3}h succeed in 106-221 ms, budget fill 80-112%, 86-100% of cells ridden once, every loop closed on the start.

External source. Of 2,237 cells where OSM knows a limit, 1,172 (52%) have a crowd p85 above it, median 1.11x. Demand is therefore recomputed at the POSTED speed, tan(theta_legal) = tan(theta_crowd)*(v_limit/v_p85)^2, dropping those cells 9.67 -> 5.60 deg. 'We never recommend speeding' becomes a term in the cost function instead of a promise on a slide.
